description: We're four Taiwan-based engineers with hands-on experience building real healthcare IT systems — hospital platforms, diabetes care tracking, and public health portals (React, Vue, Node.js, Nest.js, PostgreSQL). We also bring full-stack/enterprise frontend skills (Angular, Flutter) and AI/ML experience (TensorFlow), plus hackathon wins. Excited to apply this healthcare background to tackle astronaut health monitoring for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge.
summary:
We developed A.E.G.I.S. (Autonomous Environment & Guidance Intervention System), an offline-first health monitoring and decision-support dashboard designed for deep-space missions.

How it addresses the challenge: A.E.G.I.S. replaces passive data tables with an interactive 3D human body heatmap (Telemetry HUD). It correlates real-time environmental telemetry (e.g., ISS Live stream data for CO2, pressure) with astronaut physical training adherence to monitor fitness for duty. To prevent physiological deconditioning (e.g., bone loss, muscle atrophy), the system triggers context-aware, autonomous workflows. Instead of medical diagnoses, A.E.G.I.S. dynamically prescribes evidence-based countermeasures—such as ARED resistance and CEVIS aerobic training menus guided by NASA SP-20250000273—directly to the crew. Furthermore, A.E.G.I.S. features robust export capabilities, packaging all health records, exercise logs, and environmental snapshots into standardized HL7 FHIR formats for seamless transmission to ground medical teams.

Why it is important: During Mars missions with 20-minute communication delays, astronauts cannot wait for Houston’s directives. A.E.G.I.S. shifts the paradigm from reactive telemedicine to Earth-independent autonomy, ensuring crews maintain peak physical conditioning and remain mission-ready in isolation, while maintaining critical data continuity with Earth.
details:
How the Project is Creative

Our creativity lies in transforming a medical diagnostic tool into a Preventive Countermeasure Engine. Rather than attempting to diagnose illnesses or prescribe medications—which breaches operational safety boundaries—A.E.G.I.S. prescribes evidence-based lifestyle and nutritional adjustments.

Additionally, we gamified the data collection process. We eliminated tedious medical forms, replacing them with daily micro-tasks that capture critical subjective data (like mood and fatigue) in seconds. We also introduced "context-aware dynamic thresholds"; the system understands that physiological baselines shift in microgravity over time, automatically adjusting warning thresholds based on the specific mission day and gravity environment rather than relying on static Earth-based clinical limits.
